subject: Brightlane tax settlement & VATID proofing
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@brightlane.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@brightlane.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Invoice INV-3384 — VAT mismatch and payment timing

Hi Hannah,

Sending across invoice INV-3384 for November usage — attached. Our AP team picked up that the VAT number printed on the invoice doesn't match the one currently in VIES for Brightlane (we're registered in IE but the number on the PDF looks like an old GB registration). Finance is flagging this on their end and are asking for direction:

- Do you need us to reissue a corrected invoice from our side?
- Or can Redwood treat this as a reverse-charge (net invoice) and accept our VAT proof so payment can proceed?

We're short on cash for this cycle and a hold will push planned payroll timing — if there's a faster path (self-billing letter, corrected invoice, or a one-off acceptance of the certificate) we'd appreciate it.

I've attached our VAT registration card for quick reference. If you need a formal certificate or a VIES printout let me know.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Geller
Head of Finance, Brightlane Analytics
alex.geller@brightlane.com
+44 20 7946 0812

Attachments: Brightlane_INV-3384.pdf, Brightlane_EU_VAT_cert.jpg

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-3384 — VAT mismatch and payment timing

Thanks for the invoice and the certificate, Alex — I can triage this from our side. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Monica (finance ops).

Quick outline of options so we can agree next steps today:

1) Reissue from Brightlane
   - Cleanest: Brightlane reissues INV-3384 with the correct Irish VAT number format (IE1234567A). Redwood will accept as gross invoiced amount if VAT is charged correctly.

2) Reverse-charge / net invoicing
   - If place-of-supply is Brightlane's EU business and you provide a valid EU VAT ID, Redwood can issue a net (reverse-charge) invoice and supply a self-billing acceptance if needed. We will need the VIES validation string or an official VAT certificate PDF.

3) Self-billing authorization
   - If Brightlane signs our self-billing authorization we can reissue as a net invoice and pay on the normal schedule. This is faster than a reissue from your billing team in a lot of cases.

Monica — can you confirm which documentation we need to unblock payment immediately (VIES screenshot OK? signed cert?) and whether we should reissue from our side or ask Brightlane to reissue?

Alex — what's the latest date you need payment by to avoid the payroll issue? If you can send the VIES validation link / screenshot now that's usually enough for our initial unblock while we do the file audit.

Hannah
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Hannah.Schmitt@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-3384 — VAT mismatch and payment timing

Thanks — I pulled the invoice and the cert. Technical notes / next steps from finance ops: 

- The invoice shows VAT charged at 23% and a registration number that appears to be a UK format (GB999999973). For an Irish-registered business we need IE########A (or equivalent).
- VIES validation is acceptable evidence for us to treat this as a business-to-business supply. If Alex can provide the VIES validation token or a screenshot that shows the VAT number and "Valid" result, we can proceed to 1) reclassify the invoice as reverse-charge in our ledger and 2) push payment through on the standard NET30 if there are no other holds.

Checklist to clear the hold immediately: 
- Brightlane to confirm the correct VAT number in the body of an email (simple confirmation from Alex or AP).
- Attach the VIES validation output (screenshot or printable result).
- If Brightlane prefers Redwood to self-bill, we need a signed self-billing authorization (DocuSign link below). That will allow us to reissue a net invoice from our system without waiting for your billing team.

DocuSign (self-billing auth): https://docusign.com/r/REDACTED-selfb
Once we have the VIES screenshot + short confirmation we will:
- Reclassify INV-3384 as reverse-charge in our ledger (no VAT collected)
- Reissue a clearing invoice from Redwood that references your original INV-3384 for audit trail
- Release payment to your original payment account by EOD next business day after reclassification

Ben — FYI on the payment timeline if we follow the reverse-charge route.

Monica Patel
Revenue Operations 
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: VIES_lookup_screenshot.png

From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@brightlane.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@brightlane.com>, Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@brightlane.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 16:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-3384 — VAT mismatch and payment timing

Hi Monica / Hannah,

Thanks — confirmed: our correct VAT is IE 1234567A (we recently moved some contracts to an Irish entity and the old GB number was accidentally left on the exporter template). I've attached a fresh PDF of our official certificate and a VIES screenshot showing "Valid" and the IE number.

We are comfortable with Redwood reclassifying as reverse-charge and issuing a net clearing invoice — that will work fastest for us. We do not need a self-billing authorization signed at this time (happy to do that for future months if it helps).

Can you please confirm the expected pay date after reissue? If you can target EOD Thursday (2026-12-03) that keeps our payroll plan intact.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex

Attachments: Brightlane_EU_VAT_cert.jpg, VIES_lookup_screenshot.png
